title: Whole-string law-column audit: all three observations
instructions: Inputs, expected output, actual output and differences are shown in order. The agent evaluates the returned claims against the saved source image. Comments are optional; this is not a permission request. Enter your name to comment, Save draft to keep unfinished feedback, or Submit review to send it.

evidence.label: 1 · Inputs: original text, image and older model proposal
evidence.text:
The compact audit receives four source targets in two law columns. All original target text, the image and the complete older proposal are retained. The model is asked to report source-supported discrepancies and inspection coverage for every target; this is an audit, not a new corrected transcription. The following are exact excerpts for orientation, in original OCR then older-proposal order:

Chap. CCCXLI.—An Act to remove the Office

The compact source input, image, original words and older proposal are preserved. Relative to T118, only four text patterns in the response schema change to explicitly permit whole strings. Source content, instructions, model and options are identical. The lean reply keeps one coverage record and concise source-bound concerns per target. Independent decoding restores the original source content, keeping the reply format explicit. Expected answers below were saved separately before these calls and were not inserted into the model prompt.

evidence.text:
Run 1 — The first changed-schema reply now contains full words and explanations, unlike all three T118single-character replies. It correctly proposes joining the saved with- out to without. It still misses the wrong chapter numeral, includes two unchanged readings as concerns, and attributes tte/as maybe defects to the saved proposal even though those quotes do not occur there. Host validation rejects the no-ops; independent quote checks also reject the two wrong-layer claims. This is useful partial recognition but not a valid complete audit.

Run 2 — Second changed-schema reply again uses full phrases and finds the saved split-word defect. It explicitly claims the chapter is CCCXLI, citing the prior proposal, but the scan reads CCCXI: this repeats the historical wrong number rather than correcting it. It also reports two unchanged readings as concerns, so host validation rejects the reply. Other P4raw-word/spacing/punctuation repairs are supported by the visible print, but do not make the wrong chapter or full-coverage claim reliable.

Run 3 — Third changed-schema reply uses full phrases and again proposes the supported without reading. It flags the saved chapter but replaces CCCXLI with another wrong numeral, CCCXL; the scan reads CCCXI. Its explanation also misstates the numerical values. It includes three unchanged readings as concerns and misassigns one continuation quote to P1. Host validation rejects no-ops first; separate quote checks document source/layer failures. The three observations show better text length but zero valid complete audits and no correct selected chapter correction.

All three planned observations are saved. Every reply is retained, including disagreements and invalid results.

The detailed assessment records each source check and any extra finding. Software format checks, model self-reports, source-image AI assessment and human judgment remain separate. Agreement between repeated calls alone is not accuracy. Original sources, older proposals and human answers are unchanged.

evidence.label: 5 · Costs, capacity and remaining limits
evidence.text: Observed request cycles total 420.42 seconds. Known reported usage totals 32,895 input and 1,103 output tokens; 0 calls have unknown usage. Each call retains the 300-second lifecycle allowance and 1,500-token output cap.
